title: How self-driving cars see
examples: How do self-driving cars know where everything is?
What is the difference between radar and lidar?
Can cameras alone help a car drive safely?

explain.say: A car needs to see everything around it to drive safely.
Cameras take pictures just like your phone camera does.
Radar sends out radio waves to measure distance and speed.
Lidar sends out laser beams to create a precise 3d map.
Artificial intelligence combines all this data to understand the scene.
In real life, a self-driving car uses all three sensors together.

faq.q: Do self-driving cars rely only on cameras?
faq.a: No, they use multiple sensors like radar and lidar too. Combining data makes them much safer and more reliable.
asks: Are cameras enough for self-driving cars?
What if the camera is dirty?

faq.q: What is the main difference between radar and lidar?
faq.a: Radar uses radio waves to measure distance and speed. Lidar uses laser beams to create a very detailed 3D map of the surroundings.
asks: How does lidar work compared to radar?

faq.q: How does the car know what an object is?
faq.a: The artificial intelligence system processes the data from all sensors. It learns to recognize patterns, like the shape of a pedestrian or a stop sign.
asks: Does the car 'see' like a person?
What makes the AI smart enough?

faq.q: Can these systems work in bad weather?
faq.a: Some sensors work better in bad weather than others. For example, radar can sometimes see through fog better than cameras.

faq.q: What is a point cloud in lidar?
faq.a: A point cloud is a massive collection of millions of precise 3d coordinates. These points build a detailed digital model of everything around the car.

facts: Cameras capture visual information, similar to human eyesight.
Radar measures the range and velocity of objects using radio waves.
Lidar emits laser pulses to generate precise distance measurements.
Artificial intelligence combines these sensor inputs for decision-making.

quiz.say: If a car needs to know the exact shape of a curb, which sensor is most helpful?
quiz.why: Lidar creates a detailed 3d map using laser beams, which is perfect for mapping shapes like curbs.

wrong.0: Radar is better for speed and distance over long ranges, not fine details.
wrong.1: AI is the brain that interprets the data, not the sensor that collects the shape information.
wrong.3: Cameras are great for color but might struggle with precise depth measurements of small objects.

quiz.say: Which sensor is best for measuring how fast a car is approaching?
quiz.why: Radar is specifically designed to measure the speed and distance of objects using radio waves.

wrong.0: Cameras can estimate speed, but radar measures it directly and accurately.
wrong.1: AI uses the data from radar; it does not generate the speed measurement itself.
wrong.3: While lidar measures distance, radar is optimized for rapid speed detection.

quiz.say: When a self-driving car encounters a complex intersection, what is the most important function?
quiz.why: The car must use all sensors together, processed by AI, to form a complete understanding of the scene.

wrong.0: Relying only on cameras leaves the car vulnerable to poor lighting or weather conditions.
wrong.1: Lidar provides shape but lacks the color and context that cameras provide.
wrong.2: Radar is excellent for distance but cannot tell the car if an object is a person or a box.
